name: Illinois
dueDateNotes: Illinois follows the federal schedule: April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15.
selfEmploymentNotes: Illinois taxes your federal adjusted gross income at a flat 4.95%. It also allows a personal exemption allowance (about $2,850 per person) that is not reflected here, so your actual Illinois tax may be slightly lower.
uniqueFacts: Illinois has a flat 4.95% income tax, so every dollar of your self-employment profit is taxed at the same state rate.
Illinois requires estimated payments once you expect to owe more than $1,000 in state tax after withholding.
Illinois does not tax retirement income, but that break does not apply to your self-employment earnings.
